Knowledge packs — online fetch and air-gapped upload

Keep release notes, the Upgrade Advisory, upgrade paths and the API knowledge of builds you do not run current — a daily fetch from the knowledge feed on online nodes, a signed file upload on air-gapped ones.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage
📍 WhereSettings → System → Software Update → Knowledge packs (URL /self-update/#knowledge-packs); shell: satom show knowledge, satom execute knowledge fetch

What is it?#

SATOM no longer reads vendor web sites. Release notes, the Upgrade Advisory, upgrade paths, the API knowledge of firmware builds none of your appliances runs, and signature metadata come from signed packs, in two lanes with the same sections:

Lane What it is How it arrives
API pack Pinned to a SATOM release (satom-apipack-<version>) Inside the update; imported by the update on the primary
Knowledge pack Rolling (satom-apipack-kb-YYYYMMDD[.N]), published whenever the knowledge changes The knowledge feed, or an upload

The Knowledge packs card on Software Update shows what is installed per lane and what the feed offers, and lets you check, download and import.

What does it do?#

  • Shows, per lane, the pack installed on this node, its Date and Age, with a stale badge after 30 days. When the release's API pack was not imported because an imported pack already holds the same or newer content, the API pack row names the release's pack with covered by that pack and takes its date.
  • Check now reads the feed (latest.json) and compares it with the newest imported knowledge pack. Nothing is downloaded.
  • Download fetches the pack into the upload area. Its size and sha256 must match the feed, or nothing is kept.
  • Import downloads it if needed and imports it as a background job. The signature is verified with the knowledge lane's keys (Pack trust); a pack those keys did not sign is refused and nothing is imported.
  • Runs the daily scheduled action knowledge_fetch, whose behaviour you choose with Scheduled fetch (daily).

Requirements#

  • SATOM 3.0 or newer.
  • For the feed: outbound HTTPS from the primary to the feed, directly or through the proxy the system-upgrade feed uses. The default feed is the public knowledge release of the SATOM repository; any https:// mirror works.
  • The scheduled action knowledge_fetch must exist for the daily fetch (see How to use). The buttons work without it.

Permissions#

Everything on the card needs users.manage. Users without it do not see Software Update. The read-only console command satom show knowledge needs no web permission; satom execute knowledge fetch runs as root.

How to use#

Arm the daily fetch#

Scheduled actions are data, not code: an update does not create them. Once, on the primary:

sudo satom execute seed actions          # shows the plan
sudo satom execute seed actions --yes    # creates what is missing

It creates only the missing rows — knowledge_fetch (daily, 04:20) and the other recommended actions — and never touches rows you edited.

Choose what the daily action does#

  1. Open Software Update → Knowledge packs.
  2. Under Scheduled fetch (daily) pick a mode.
  3. Optionally set Feed URL (empty = the default feed).
  4. Click Save. The page confirms "Knowledge fetch mode set to …".

Pull a pack now#

  1. Click Check now. The card shows what Available from the feed offers.
  2. Click Import (or Download to stage it only).
  3. Follow the job; when it ends, the Installed row of the knowledge lane shows the new pack.

Air-gapped network#

  1. On a machine with Internet access, download the pack named by the feed and its .sha256 file from the knowledge release of the SATOM repository (after Check now, the card links both).
  2. Verify it: sha256sum -c satom-apipack-kb-<date>.tar.gz.sha256.
  3. Carry the file over. On the primary, upload it under API library packs (/self-update/apipack/upload) and import it there — or run sudo satom execute apipack import ./satom-apipack-kb-<date>.tar.gz --yes.

The signature check is the same as online.

From the console#

satom show knowledge                                  # installed per lane, age, mode, last result
sudo satom execute knowledge fetch                    # check only (dry run)
sudo satom execute knowledge fetch --yes              # download and stage
sudo satom execute knowledge fetch --import --yes     # download and import
sudo satom execute knowledge fetch --feed https://mirror.example/latest.json --import --yes

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Scheduled fetch (daily) off — nothing; notify — check and tell the administrators (bell) once per new pack; download — also download and stage; download_import — also import (default) Yes download_import
Feed URL The feed (latest.json). Must be https://. Empty = the public default feed No https://mirror.example/satom/knowledge/latest.json

Both settings are replicated: change them on the primary.

Example#

🧪Example — An online pair

After updating both nodes to 3.0, the administrator runs sudo satom execute seed actions --yes on the primary. The next morning knowledge_fetch finds satom-apipack-kb-20261012, downloads it, checks its sha256, verifies its signature with the knowledge key and imports it. The standby receives the data by replication. The Release Notes window now reads Knowledge from satom-apipack-kb-20261012 (2026-10-12).

Result#

  • An import adds what the node does not hold and replaces copies an earlier pack wrote when the new pack is built from a newer snapshot. What this node measured or wrote itself is never replaced.
  • Every imported row records its provenance: pack:knowledge:<pack> or pack:api_pack:<pack>.
  • The last result (status, message, time, pack) is shown under the table (Last check:).
  • Changing the settings is audited as knowledge.settings.

Troubleshooting#

"This node is the STANDBY: its database is read-only. Knowledge packs are fetched and imported on the PRIMARY and arrive here by replication."#

Possible causes - You are on the standby.

Solution 1. Open Software Update on the primary.

"Knowledge settings are replicated — change them on the PRIMARY node (this node's database is read-only)."#

Same cause: save the mode and feed URL on the primary.

"Knowledge settings not saved: the feed URL must be https://"#

Solution 1. Enter an https:// URL, or leave the field empty for the default feed.

"the knowledge feed is not JSON" / "the feed carries no valid sha256 for …"#

Possible causes - The Feed URL does not point at a knowledge latest.json (a proxy error page, a wrong path on a mirror).

Solution 1. Open the URL from the node with curl and check that it returns the JSON. 2. Fix the URL or the mirror.

"… sha256 on disk does not match the feed"#

Possible causes - The download was truncated or altered in transit; nothing was kept.

Solution 1. Click Download again. If it repeats, check the proxy.

"this knowledge pack is not signed by a trusted knowledge key …"#

Possible causes - The file is not an official knowledge pack, or it was signed with another lane's key.

Solution 1. Compare the fingerprint with the published one (Pack trust). Never add a key you cannot verify.

The Installed row shows "stale"#

Possible causes - The mode is off or notify, the action does not exist, or the feed is unreachable.

Solution 1. Check Last check: for the reason. 2. Arm the action (satom execute seed actions --yes) or import by hand.

Advanced#

Advanced How the feed is trusted

The feed is an address book, not a reason to trust anything. A forged latest.json can at most point at a pack no trusted key signed, and that pack is refused by the import. The HTTP client is the system-upgrade feed's: HTTPS only (redirects included), the process proxy environment, the system CA store and a size cap. notify tells the administrators once per new pack version, not once per day.

Advanced Which pack wins

Local data always wins. Between packs, the newer snapshot wins whatever its lane, so a knowledge pack can correct something the release's API pack carried without waiting for the next release. Only when the snapshot time is unknown (a copy a 2.x pack wrote) or equal does the API pack outrank the knowledge pack. See API library.
